announcements.name: Copy Flag named 2026 Imagine Cup World Champion
announcements.shortDescription: Patrick Brown's AI defense platform for creators won the top prize.
announcements.longDescription: CopyFlag was announced as the 2026 Imagine Cup World Champion, selected over two other finalist startups. Founded by Patrick Brown, CopyFlag is an AI-powered platform that helps independent creators turn the invisible problem of AI-modified copyright infringement into a visible, actionable one. The win was announced by Hans Yang alongside Dona Sarkar.

announcements.name: Grand prize increased from $100,000 to $150,000
announcements.shortDescription: Microsoft surprised the finalists by raising the award on stage.
announcements.longDescription: As a surprise to the finalists, Microsoft announced that it was backing the founders more than ever before by raising the Imagine Cup grand prize from $100,000 to $150,000. The increase was revealed on stage just before the World Champion was named.

announcements.name: Mentoring session with Satya Nadella
announcements.shortDescription: The champion receives a one-on-one mentorship with Microsoft's Chairman and CEO.
announcements.longDescription: Dona Sarkar explained that the Imagine Cup grand prize includes $100,000 and a mentoring session with Satya Nadella himself. This mentorship was described as a key part of what was at stake for the competing founders.

announcements.name: Three finalists selected from over 1,000 submissions
announcements.shortDescription: Copy Flag, Spoilsafe, and Revora Health advanced to the world championship.
announcements.longDescription: Dona Sarkar announced that three startups rose to the top from over 8,000 submissions to advance to the Imagine Cup World Championship, where they pitched to a panel of judges. This year's journey was shaped by Microsoft for Startups along with partners at GitHub Education and Replit, and founders were matched with industry-leading mentors. The judges were Dr. Irina Raicu, Bakari Brock, and Thea Myhrvold.
